title: China moves to curb tech exports, including AI, citing national security risks
source_used: Associated Press (text read in the PBS NewsHour copy)
key_facts: On Friday 16 Oct 2026 China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology jointly published a draft update to the catalog of technologies subject to export bans or restrictions.

The draft covers 40 technologies spanning artificial intelligence, chips and solar power; 23 are AI technologies, from advanced large models to agents, and the list also has 12 solar and five biomedicine technologies.

Exports of core technologies of AI large models trained on sensitive national data would be prohibited, as would AI agents designed for highly sensitive uses such as national defense and critical information infrastructure.
Exports of AI models with 2 trillion or more parameters, or with certain world-leading capabilities, could be restricted; the proposal does not name specific models.
Several chip design technologies, including for some AI processing chips and memory chips, are also on the list.
A commerce ministry spokesperson called the move necessary and cited national security; the statement says the aims include preventing misuse and ensuring AI stays under human control.
The proposal came as China and the US made progress in talks on AI safety and on a mechanism to notify each other of AI incidents that could threaten national security.
Lian Jye Su, a chief analyst at research firm Omdia, sees it as a response to Western countries' sovereignty demands on AI, robotics and telecoms technologies.
quote_evidence: China on Friday said it plans to restrict or ban exports of 40 technologies that span artificial intelligence, chips and solar power as its technology race with countries including the United States intensifies.

The Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology jointly published a draft document with the proposed updates for China's catalog of technologies subjected to export bans or restrictions.
Twenty-three AI technologies, from advanced large models to agents, are included on Friday's list, according to the Chinese ministries.
why_it_matters_hint: China's draft could cut off foreign access to Chinese AI models, chips and solar know-how, deepening the technology split with the US.
